title: Exact runtime for computing query flags
statement: Let $l,N,W,U$ be natural numbers, let $p,n\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, let $r_s(i)$ be a family of bit words, let $y_0,y_1$ be target bit words, and let $v$ be a bit-word tail. Suppose $|r_s(i)|\le W$ for every $s<N$ and every $i$, $|y_j|\le W$ for each $j\in\{0,1\}$, and each query word formed from the targets, the stream of packed rows followed by $v$, and the unary clock of length $N$ has length at most $U$. Then the finite binary query machine on the packed query argument $a$ halts within $2|a|+9+(l+5)(3U+7)+N(l(5W+7)+2W+7)$ steps and outputs, in source-time order, the $N$ Boolean flags indicating whether $r_s(p)+y_1=r_s(n)+y_0$, with each word interpreted as a little-endian binary numeral.
hypotheses_covered: $p,n$ are coordinates in a set of size $l$ and are distinct
$r_s(i)$ is a family of bit words
all row words with $s<N$ have length at most $W$
both target words have length at most $W$
all query words have length at most $U$
replaced: For distinct coordinates, a row family with fields of length at most $W$ among the first $N$ rows, target words of length at most $W$, a trailer, and argument words of length at most $U$, the query transducer computes, from the packed encoding of the query argument, exactly the list of the $N$ comparison flags in source-time order, within $2|a| + 9 + (l+5)(3U+7) + N(l(5W+7) + 2W + 7)$ steps, where $a$ is the argument; argument copying, preparation, every row query, comparison, dispatch, flag write, rewind, replay, and the halt are all charged.
